lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
- Cut the booking flow's JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Moving image resizing to the CDN, inlining critical CSS, preloading the two web fonts and deferring the analytics script, raised the checkout page's Lighthouse performance score from 52 to 91.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Documented the design-system tokens in Storybook so designers could check spacing and color values without asking engineers.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Apr 2024 - Aug 2024
- Cut the university sites' JavaScript bundle by 60% by converting their PNG images to WebP.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cut cold-start time on slow 3G from 3.0s to 1.5s, a 75% improvement, by caching the stop list offline.
- Raised weekly returning riders by 10% in the first month, from 30% to 40%, by adding saved stops.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Presented the demo to the library staff and handed over the code with setup notes.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The code URL appears to be a placeholder and should be replaced with a real, clickable link.
items.because: Recruiters should not have to infer where the work is hosted.

items.says: Add LinkedIn if the profile is professionally complete.
items.because: It could be useful for a graduate student applying to software roles.

items.says: Consider adding a relevant specialization, concentration, or selected coursework.
items.because: It could help for frontend, web performance, accessibility, or systems-oriented roles.

items.says: Consider including GPA if it is strong and customary for the target roles.
Make the undergraduate entry's formatting clearly consistent with the graduate entry.
items.because: Both degrees are from the same university, and the section should be easy to scan.

items.says: Clarify the scope of the A/B test behind the 9% increase.
items.because: A recruiter may want to know its significance, sample size, or primary success metric.

items.says: Specify your ownership of the server-side rendering work.
items.because: The bullet should not imply you implemented more of it than you did.

items.says: Tie the JavaScript reduction to an observable result or clarify its measurement context.
items.because: That would make the reduction's importance clearer.

items.says: Verify that the 410 KB and 260 KB sizes were measured consistently.
items.because: Different compression or initial-versus-total measurements could make the result misleading.

items.says: Replace “screen-reader labels” with the specific accessibility work performed.
items.because: The phrase is broad and could refer to names, focus management, announcements, or semantics.

items.says: Clarify what “all 14 accessibility issues” covers.
items.because: The issues may have been limited to the component or page rather than the whole product.

items.says: Name the accessibility standard or audit source if useful.
items.because: A recognized standard or process would make the result more credible.

items.says: Fix the sentence structure and clarify which changes you made.
items.because: The sequence of actions followed by “raised” obscures the subject and attribution.

items.says: Verify that the two Lighthouse scores were measured under comparable conditions.
items.because: Different devices, networks, versions, or page states could make the increase incomparable.

items.says: Confirm that font preloading contributed to a measured improvement.
items.because: Preloading fonts can help or hurt performance depending on their importance and usage.

items.says: Investigate whether lazy-loading the hero image caused the LCP improvement.
items.because: A hero image is often the LCP element, and lazy-loading it can delay LCP.

items.says: Do not attribute the entire LCP improvement to one change unless it was measured separately.
items.because: Multiple changes may have contributed to the result.

items.says: Add the scope or a result of the Storybook documentation.
items.because: The bullet currently ends at the activity rather than showing its impact.

items.says: Clarify whether designers actually used the documentation.
items.because: “So designers could check” describes intent, not measured adoption or reduced back-and-forth.

items.says: Converting PNG images to WebP cannot by itself reduce a JavaScript bundle.
items.because: Image format changes affect image payload size, not JavaScript bundle size.

items.says: Specify what the 60% reduction measured and which sites it covered.
items.because: The plural “sites” makes the measurement scope important.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the preview mode.
items.because: The wording shows that research led to the feature but not whether you designed or implemented it.

items.says: Define “broken pages” and the source and periods of the before-and-after figures.
items.because: The metric may come from informal reports, and the periods should be comparable.

items.says: “Writes” uses present tense for a role that ended in August 2024.
items.because: Completed roles should use consistent past tense unless the work continues separately.

items.says: Clarify your level of ownership of the accessibility checklist.
items.because: The wording suggests an ongoing institutional responsibility that may not reflect your role.

items.says: Identify what kind of audits the failure counts refer to.
items.because: “Failed audits” could mean automated checks, manual reviews, or formal compliance reviews.

items.says: Explain what “search time” measures.
items.because: It could mean filtering latency, task completion time, or perceived response time.

items.says: Check whether “client-side filtering” accurately describes the architecture.
items.because: The description depends on how much of the dataset was downloaded to the browser.

items.says: Add the scope of the search improvement if available.
items.because: The number of courses, users, or searches would establish its significance.

items.says: Distinguish ongoing project work from results achieved in its first month.
items.because: The project is dated “Present.”

items.says: Clarify how the estimate of 900 weekly riders was measured.
items.because: It could represent unique users, sessions, or riders estimated another way, and should be current and reproducible.

items.says: Add relevant deployment or data-source details if space permits.
items.because: The transit API, hosting, PWA features, or monitoring could make a live app more compelling.

items.says: Calling a drop from 3.0 seconds to 1.5 seconds a 75% improvement is incorrect.
items.because: It is a 50% reduction.

items.says: Explain how offline caching improved the stated cold-start scenario.
items.because: Caching may help subsequent loads but not necessarily a first-ever cold start.

items.says: The change from 30% to 40% is mislabeled as a 10% increase.
items.because: It is 10 percentage points, or approximately a 33% relative increase.

items.says: Include TypeScript consistently in the project's technology list if it was used.
items.because: The project bullet lists TypeScript, but the technology line does not.

items.says: The React claim contradicts the project's Vue label.
items.because: The résumé does not explain which framework was used or whether both were used.

items.says: Replace “Worked on the frontend” with your specific contribution.
items.because: The phrase is generic, while the calendar bullet implies more specific ownership.

items.says: Explain the outcome of the handoff if available.
items.because: Adoption or use by library staff would make the presentation and setup notes more impactful.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: It should be “Storybook.”

items.says: Reconsider listing Angular if you cannot discuss meaningful experience with it.
items.because: Angular appears nowhere else in the résumé.

items.says: Add relevant tools demonstrated by the experience, if applicable.
items.because: Testing, performance, CI/CD, or cloud and CDN tools could be useful without creating an unsupported inventory.

items.says: Separate technical areas from practices in the Methods category.
items.because: Accessibility and server-side rendering are areas of expertise, while component testing is a practice.

items.says: Make the strongest frontend results the visual and content focus.
items.because: Performance, accessibility, experimentation, and user-facing improvements are the résumé's best themes.

items.says: Apply punctuation and formatting choices consistently throughout.
items.because: Bullets, dates, locations, technology separators, and titles should follow a consistent style.

items.says: Add evidence of broader engineering work if targeting general software engineering roles and that evidence exists.
items.because: The current content is positioned primarily toward frontend roles.
